pointers.sentence: The module is imported when something first asks the resolver for it, through `urlconf_module`, a property that keeps on the resolver the first value it computes; an import that raises computes none (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.urlconf_module`).

`include` imports a module it is given by name before it returns, so each included module is imported in the middle of the root's own import, at the first `include` that names it, and an `include` that names a module already imported runs none of its code again (`django/urls/conf.py:include`).

Asked for again, `get_resolver` returns the same resolver from its cache, with its list already on it, and nothing is imported or built a second time (`django/urls/resolvers.py:get_resolver`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:_get_cached_resolver`).

Asked for again, `get_resolver` returns the same resolver from its cache, with its list already on it, and nothing is imported or built a second time (`django/urls/resolvers.py:get_resolver`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:_get_cached_resolver`).
`get_wsgi_application` loads the settings and the applications and makes the handler, and none of that touches the URLconf (`django/core/wsgi.py:get_wsgi_application`).

`URLResolver.resolve` reads `URLResolver.url_patterns` for the first path that reaches it, unless something in the request has needed the URLconf sooner: `LocaleMiddleware.process_request` has `url_patterns` read to learn whether the URLconf has a language prefix ([Language prefixes and translated routes](i18n.md)), and when an exception raised in a middleware is to be answered by an error view, `URLResolver.resolve_error_handler` reads the URLconf's module to look for one (`django/conf/urls/i18n.py:is_language_prefix_patterns_used`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.resolve_error_handler`).

The check `check_url_config` asks the root resolver to check itself, and `URLResolver.check` goes through `url_patterns` to do it, so a command such as runserver imports the whole tree before it does its work ([The URL checks, and listing the patterns](checks.md), [The system checks](../commands/checks.md)) (`django/core/checks/urls.py:check_url_config`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.check`).

Under runserver the autoreloader reads `URLResolver.urlconf_module` as well, in `BaseReloader.run`, as soon as the applications are ready, so that the URL modules are already loaded when the reloader starts; if the import raises, it stores the exception and carries on ([The autoreloader](../commands/autoreload.md)) (`django/utils/autoreload.py:BaseReloader.run`).
The first call of `reverse` reads the list too, to build its tables ([Reversing a name](reversing.md#the-tables)) (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver._populate`).

The second `ImportError` is raised inside the wrapper's own handling of the first, and nothing in that wrapper catches it (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:convert_exception_to_response`, `django/core/handlers/exception.py:handle_uncaught_exception`).

The second `ImportError` is raised inside the wrapper's own handling of the first, and nothing in that wrapper catches it (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:convert_exception_to_response`, `django/core/handlers/exception.py:handle_uncaught_exception`).

And the thread keeps the current URLconf the handler set for the request, since what clears it is the closing of a response, and there was none ([The script prefix, the current URLconf and the caches](state.md#the-current-urlconf)) (`django/core/handlers/base.py:reset_urlconf`).

The debug page is made without any error view, but it names the view that was handling the request, and for a request that has no match yet it resolves the path to find out, so the import is tried a second time inside the code that builds the page ([The debug pages and `ExceptionReporter`](../views/debug.md)) (`django/views/debug.py:get_caller`).

`URLResolver.url_patterns` then has a module in place of a list, cannot iterate it, and raises `ImproperlyConfigured`; the exception ends the import, and the module leaves `sys.modules` but stays on the resolver (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.urlconf_module`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.url_patterns`).

The resolver keeps the half-made module, so every later read of `url_patterns`, for a path or for `reverse`, raises the same `ImproperlyConfigured` without trying the import again (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.url_patterns`).
